For every call to withdrawAll(recipient), only the address set as owner at construction may successfully execute the withdrawal (i.e., withdrawAll only succeeds when msg.sender == owner); the mutant that checks tx.origin instead of msg.sender allows a non-owner contract caller to withdraw when tx.origin == owner, violating this rule for some inputs.
Only the stored owner can cause the contract to send its entire balance to an arbitrary recipient (i.e., withdrawAll succeeds only when msg.sender equals c.owner()).

property_summary: When withdrawAll succeeds (does not revert) the caller does not receive the contract's funds (i.e., the call does not result in msg.sender receiving the contract balance).
If withdrawAll succeeds then the caller is not the recipient of the withdrawn funds (i.e., the caller's address does not get the contract's balance as a result).

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) on the correct contract transfers the contract's entire balance to the specified recipient (so afterwards address(c).balance == 0), while the mutated version sends funds to msg.sender causing some inputs (recipient != owner and nonzero balance) to leave recipient unfunded and still satisfy address(c).balance == 0 but the intended recipient did not receive funds — we assert that after the call the contract balance is zero (reference holds for all inputs; mutant still makes balance zero but breaks recipient delivery), so instead we assert that the recipient's balance increases by the contract balance amount which the reference guarantees and the mutant violates when recipient != owner.

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the contract's entire balance to that recipient (recipient balance increases by the contract's previous balance); the mutant that sends funds to msg.sender instead breaks this whenever recipient != owner and contract has nonzero balance.

For any owner caller and any recipient address when the contract holds some ether, calling withdrawAll(recipient) always results in the recipient's balance increasing by the contract's entire pre-call balance; the mutant that sends to msg.sender breaks this when recipient != owner (recipient does not get the funds).

If the caller is the owner, then after withdrawAll(recipient) completes the contract's balance is zero and the recipient's balance increases by the contract's entire pre-call balance when recipient is a contract that can receive ether; the mutant that sends to msg.sender instead will not increase that recipient's balance when recipient != owner, so the property will fail for some fuzzed recipient address.

After withdrawAll is called by the owner, the recipient's balance increases by the contract balance prior to the call (i.e., funds are transferred to the supplied recipient, not necessarily to owner).

For any caller equal to owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) on the reference always transfers the contract's entire balance out (so address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that additionally requires recipient == owner prevents draining to other recipients, leaving address(c).balance > 0 for some recipient inputs.

For any caller equal to owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) on the reference always transfers out the contract balance (so address(c).balance == 0 after the call); the mutant that requires recipient==owner prevents draining when owner calls with a different recipient, leaving address(c).balance > 0 for some recipient inputs.
